properties.state: {"concern":"core","kind":"functional","lineage":"original","name":"Every operation that reads a second design (compare, compose, merge, fork_point, pairing, seam coverage, topic compare, chunk take) takes its other designs BY GRAPH_ID, served by the registry over the designs one process holds, and the host passes the set the caller may read","priority":"high","provenance":"authored","source":"Anthony Sligar (who:ajs), dev_reflow2 hub session 2026-10-10","statement":"Every reflow2 operation whose input is more than one design — compare_designs, compose_and_analyse, merge_designs, fork_point, pair_designs, seam_coverage, and the compare-on-one-topic, seam-gaps and chunk-take operations already accepted — SHALL accept its other design(s) by graph_id as well as by path. By graph_id the registry (cap:graph-registry) resolves each to the DesignGraph the process already holds, opening on demand as it does for a single design, so a hosted server can serve the whole family where today it withholds every by-path tool. The host SHALL pass the set of graph_ids the caller may read on every such call; a graph_id outside that set is left out of the result and the reply says it was left out, never what it held. An operation that WRITES to a second design takes its write locks in one fixed order or refuses, so two cross-design writes cannot deadlock the registry. The result returned is the difference, the candidates or the assembled analysis — never a second design's contents for the agent to diff itself. ORDER OF BUILD (kept as the first step): compare_designs and compose_and_analyse first, measured on flo2.io's registry (open cost once, scan cost per call) before the rest of the family is widened. Settled in dec:idea-cross-design-operations-are-a-primitive-layer-served-by-the-registry-by-graph-id, option (a); its pushback stands: key equality is not design equality across vocabularies, so the cross-vocabulary half remains similarity scoring returning candidates for a judgement.
